company_overview: Mid-size supply-chain optimization platform building customer-facing chat and reranking for S&OP workflows.
High emphasis on deterministic latency for agent workflows and strong data residency controls.
Prototype uses open Llama-variant for reranking + Mistral-style chat model for assistant.
technical_summary: Primary workloads: interactive chat (assistant) and high-volume embeddings + reranking for search results.
Current baseline: 20 steady QPS for chat, expected steady-state target 50 QPS after GA; peak expected 160 QPS during morning sync windows.
Average tokens per chat request: 240 tokens (user+system+history trimmed); p50 response tokens ~120, p95 ~480 depending on thread length.
Embeddings: 400 requests/min during spikes, each call 1536-dim model, negligible response size but high qps bursts after nightly ingestion.
Latency SLOs: p95 < 350ms for short-chat (<=128 input tokens), p99 < 800ms for full threads; business requires p99 SLA negotiation for core flows.
Throughput goals: baseline token/sec budget ~12k tokens/sec steady, peak token/sec budget ~40k tokens/sec for short intervals.
Availability target: 99.95% for production endpoints, with fallbacks to smaller local model variant when Dedicated pool saturated.
Data residency: must keep logs and embeddings in US-East region, customer will not accept cross-region backups without encryption key escrow.
Security: SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning required; audit logs retained 12 months; KMS integration for model request payload encryption.
Operational constraints: limited burst budget from infra cost center, require predictable reserved GPU planning with clear overage rates.
workshop_objectives: Establish steady-state QPS and token/sec baseline per workload (chat, embeddings, rerank).
Map token distributions by user cohort and identify cacheable prefixes to reduce sustained token/sec demand.
Quantify peak headroom needed for 99th/99.9th percentile latency targets and map to reserved GPU count.
Agree on acceptable fallback/routing policy (model variants, region fallback) and SLA penalty language for p99 breaches.
Produce a recommended Dedicated capacity plan (GPU types, reservation sizing, burst pool) and cost estimate.

recommended_capacity_plan_summary: Short-term (POC): Reserve 2 x p4-equivalent nodes (or 2 x 80GB GPUs) to validate latency and batching settings.
Production target: 6 reserved GPUs to meet steady 50 QPS with 2x headroom for spikes (expected p95 < 350ms).
Burst pool: 4 extra GPUs on burst contract for predictable upscaling to cover 160 QPS peaks with automated routing to lower-cost model variants when saturated.
Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for top 15% longest threads to reduce sustained token/sec by ~12-18%.
Quantization: recommend 4-bit quantized variant for background reranking jobs; keep full FP16 for interactive chat flows.
negotiation_points_and_risks: SLA: customer wants p99 across multi-region clients; Redwood recommends region-scoped SLA with documented fallback behavior.
Cost: customer prefers committed monthly GPU hours - need to finalize overage rates and burst billing cadence.
Security: KMS key escrow and audit log retention window (12 months) are negotiation items for enterprise policy.
Operational: on-call rotation and escalation (SRE contact) to be finalized; CSM to provide runbook template.
